title: Best CertainTeed shingle lines for New Hampshire homes 2026
body_markdown:
**Best overall: CertainTeed Landmark. Best for stronger color contrast: Landmark PRO. Best for a wood-shake appearance: Presidential Shake. Best for a slate-style appearance: Grand Manor.** This 2026 guide compares the best CertainTeed shingle lines for New Hampshire homes and explains what your replacement estimate should include before you choose.


**TL;DR**

- The best CertainTeed shingle lines for New Hampshire homes start with Landmark for a straightforward architectural roof replacement.
- Choose Landmark PRO for stronger color contrast, Presidential Shake for shake styling, or Grand Manor for slate styling.
- Compare tear-off, flashing, decking repairs, and ventilation before comparing the final estimate totals.
- Prescott Roofing serves Southern New Hampshire homeowners planning a residential roof replacement.


## Why this matters

A shingle selection is only part of a roof replacement. The roof deck, water-shedding details, flashing, and ventilation need attention regardless of which CertainTeed line you choose.

For your 2026 replacement, separate appearance decisions from installation decisions. A more elaborate shingle profile does not correct deteriorated decking or poorly detailed flashing. **Prescott Roofing is a residential roof replacement option for Southern New Hampshire homeowners.** You can [request an inspection from Prescott Roofing](https://prescottroofingnh.com/) to start discussing your roof; submitting a request does not mean an appointment is booked.

## What makes the best CertainTeed shingle line?

Use these criteria before looking at colors or signing an estimate:

- **Architectural fit:** Choose a conventional architectural, shake-style, or slate-style appearance that suits your house.
- **Visible difference:** Decide whether added contrast or a more pronounced profile is noticeable from the street.
- **Roof suitability:** Have the contractor check slope, roof condition, and the selected product's installation requirements.
- **Complete installation scope:** Compare tear-off, underlayment, flashing, ventilation, and cleanup alongside the shingle line.
- **Clear product identification:** Require the exact line and color in writing, not simply the CertainTeed brand name.
- **Documented exclusions:** Find out how concealed deck damage and other additional work will be handled.

## CertainTeed shingle lines at a glance

These rankings separate appearance priorities rather than pretending one shingle is right for every house. All four are asphalt shingle options; their visual styles are different.

| Shingle line | Best for | Standout feature | Key limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| CertainTeed Landmark | Straightforward architectural replacement | Dimensional wood-shake appearance | Less pronounced styling than the designer options below |
| CertainTeed Landmark PRO | Stronger color contrast | CertainTeed's Max Def color treatment | Color contrast is not a substitute for installation quality |
| CertainTeed Presidential Shake | A pronounced wood-shake look | Sculpted shake-style profile | A distinctive appearance that needs a full-roof visual check |
| CertainTeed Grand Manor | A slate-style architectural statement | Layered slate-style appearance | Its visual emphasis is unnecessary if you want an understated roof |

## 1. CertainTeed Landmark: best for a straightforward replacement

CertainTeed Landmark is an architectural asphalt shingle with a dimensional wood-shake appearance. It is the default starting point here for homeowners who want an architectural roof without making an elaborate designer profile the main decision.

**Landmark is the best overall starting point for a conventional asphalt roof replacement.** Compare the complete installation scope first, then decide whether another line's appearance justifies changing your selection.

**CertainTeed Landmark pros:**

- Dimensional styling rather than a flat, repeating three-tab appearance.
- An understated starting point for comparing more pronounced profiles.
- Keeps the selection focused when your priority is replacing the roof rather than changing the home's architectural character.

**CertainTeed Landmark cons:**

- Does not reproduce Grand Manor's slate-style appearance.
- Its profile is less pronounced than Presidential Shake's sculpted styling.

**Best for:** Homeowners who want a conventional architectural asphalt roof and a clear baseline for comparing estimates.

Ask for a physical sample against your siding and trim. A shingle viewed on a table can read differently from a roof seen across the street.

**Verdict: Buy Landmark when its appearance meets your needs and the installation scope is complete.**

## 2. CertainTeed Landmark PRO: best for stronger color contrast

CertainTeed Landmark PRO is an architectural asphalt shingle line featuring CertainTeed's Max Def color treatment. Its clearest place in this comparison is for homeowners who want more pronounced color variation while retaining an architectural shingle appearance.

For a 2026 selection, compare the actual samples rather than treating the PRO name as the decision. The question is whether you prefer the visible result on your house.

**CertainTeed Landmark PRO pros:**

- Stronger color contrast provides a distinct reason to compare it with Landmark.
- Retains an architectural shingle appearance rather than switching to slate-style design.
- Offers a middle decision path between conventional architectural styling and a more sculpted designer profile.

**CertainTeed Landmark PRO cons:**

- Strong contrast can compete with patterned brick, stone, or multicolored siding.
- The product name alone does not establish what flashing, ventilation, or deck work the estimate includes.

**Best for:** Homeowners who like architectural shingles but want the roof color to have greater visual definition.

Compare 3 sample boards outdoors: your preferred Landmark color, your preferred Landmark PRO color, and an alternative that works with the siding. This is a selection exercise, not a reason to change an otherwise suitable roof specification.

**Verdict: Buy Landmark PRO for a visible color preference, not simply because the name sounds like an upgrade.**

## 3. CertainTeed Presidential Shake: best for wood-shake styling

CertainTeed Presidential Shake is an asphalt shingle designed to create a wood-shake appearance with a pronounced, sculpted profile. It belongs on your shortlist when the roof's texture is a deliberate part of the exterior design.

A house with broad, visible roof planes gives you more opportunity to see that styling. On a roof largely hidden from ground level, decide whether the profile matters enough to your replacement plan.

**CertainTeed Presidential Shake pros:**

- A distinct shake-style appearance separates it from conventional architectural shingles.
- Pronounced texture gives the roof a stronger visual role.
- Provides a shake-inspired option without choosing actual wood roofing.

**CertainTeed Presidential Shake cons:**

- The pronounced profile is not the right aesthetic for every house.
- A small sample does not show how the repeating pattern looks across a large roof plane.

**Best for:** Homeowners deliberately choosing a textured, wood-shake-inspired exterior.

Ask to see manufacturer photography showing a complete roof in the selected line. Use those images to judge the pattern, then use physical samples to judge color; neither replaces checking the actual installation requirements.

**Verdict: Buy Presidential Shake when shake styling is a firm design priority; skip it when you want an understated roof.**

## 4. CertainTeed Grand Manor: best for a slate-style appearance

CertainTeed Grand Manor is an asphalt shingle line designed to resemble slate roofing. Its layered appearance makes it a different aesthetic choice from Landmark, Landmark PRO, and Presidential Shake.

Choose Grand Manor because you want slate-style design in an asphalt roofing system. Do not treat it as actual slate or assume that its appearance establishes the requirements for your particular roof.

**CertainTeed Grand Manor pros:**

- A slate-style appearance creates a distinct alternative to shake-inspired shingles.
- Layered styling gives visible roof planes a defined architectural role.
- Lets you compare a different design direction without changing the discussion to natural slate installation.

**CertainTeed Grand Manor cons:**

- Its visual character is unnecessary when your goal is a simple, quiet roofline.
- It remains an asphalt product, not a substitute for natural slate in every architectural specification.

**Best for:** Homeowners who specifically want a layered, slate-style roof appearance.

For a 2026 replacement, have the contractor identify the exact product and applicable installation instructions before you approve the scope. A designer appearance should come with a clearly defined installation plan, not a vague upgrade description.

**Verdict: Buy Grand Manor for intentional slate styling; skip it if that appearance is not part of your goal.**

## What your roof replacement estimate should include

Get 2 written estimates that describe comparable work. Comparing totals without comparing scope leaves you guessing about what each contractor intends to replace, retain, or exclude.

### Tear-off and deck review

Tear-off means removing existing roofing so the underlying deck can be inspected. The estimate should identify what will be removed, how debris will be handled, and how concealed deterioration will be documented.

Ask how additional deck work receives your approval. A contractor cannot fully inspect concealed decking before it is exposed, but the estimate can explain the process for dealing with it.

### Underlayment and flashing

Underlayment is the protective layer beneath the shingles. Flashing directs water away from roof intersections, penetrations, and adjoining walls; step flashing uses individual overlapping pieces where a sloped roof meets a wall.

Require the estimate to distinguish new flashing from flashing proposed for reuse. For more background on the layer beneath the shingles, compare [synthetic roofing underlayment for cold New England winters](https://prescottroofingnh.com/blog/best-synthetic-roofing-underlayment-for-cold-new-england-winters).

### Ventilation and cleanup

Ask how the contractor will assess attic intake and exhaust ventilation. Adding a roof vent without checking the rest of the airflow path is not a complete ventilation plan.

Cleanup belongs in writing too. Identify debris removal, protection of nearby surfaces, and the final walkthrough rather than assuming every estimate includes the same tasks.
